ethiopia.title: Ndakimana Tips Rwanda to Overturn Ethiopia Deficit in LA 2028 Qualifiers
ethiopia.content: East Africa: Ndakimana Tips Rwanda to Overturn Ethiopia Deficit in LA 2028 Qualifiers - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français East Africa: Ndakimana Tips Rwanda to Overturn Ethiopia Deficit in LA 2028 Qualifiers 12 October 2026 The New Times (Kigali) By Peter Kamasa Tuesday, October 13 Olympic Qualifiers (Second Leg) Ethiopia vs Rwanda (Dire Dawa Stadium, Ethiopia) Rwanda women's national team captain Angeline Ndakimana is confident that Amavubi can overturn their first-leg deficit and eliminate Ethiopia when the two sides meet in the return leg of the 2028 CAF Women's Olympic Qualifiers at Dire Dawa Stadium on Tuesday. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Rwanda head into the decisive encounter trailing 1-0 on aggregate following a heartbreaking defeat in the first leg in Kigali on October 7. Despite the setback, Ndakimana believes Amavubi have the quality and determination to respond away from home and keep their Olympic qualification hopes alive. "We made a mistake in the first leg, but we can turn things around away from home. They are a good team, but we can beat them," Ndakimana said. "We have been preparing well for this match because we know how difficult it is going to be. Everyone in the team is focused on achieving a positive result," she added. Head coach André Casa Mbungo shares his captain's optimism, insisting that the team has worked to address the shortcomings that cost them in the first leg. "We corrected our mistakes and we want to make sure that we get a good result. I know it is hard, but it is possible," Casa Mbungo said. The first leg appeared destined to end in a goalless draw before a stoppage-time own goal by Rwanda defender Lydia Uzayisenga handed Ethiopia a crucial advantage. Uzayisenga inadvertently turned Abebe Mihiret's cross into her own net in the second minute of added time, leaving Rwanda with a difficult task ahead of the return fixture. With their Olympic dream on the line, Amavubi must produce a strong performance in Ethiopia to keep their qualification campaign alive. Rwanda need to win by at least two goals to overturn the deficit and secure progression to the third round. The winner of the tie will advance to the next stage, where either Tanzania or Botswana awaits as the qualification campaign continues. Read the original article on New Times . Rwanda Hold Ethiopia but Bow Out of CAF Women's Olympic Qualifiers
ethiopia.content: Rwanda/Ethiopia: Rwanda Hold Ethiopia but Bow Out of CAF Women's Olympic Qualifiers - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Rwanda/Ethiopia: Rwanda Hold Ethiopia but Bow Out of CAF Women's Olympic Qualifiers 14 October 2026 The New Times (Kigali) By Peter Kamasa Rwanda's hopes of qualifying for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games came to an end on Tuesday after the Amavubi held Ethiopia to a 1-1 draw in the second leg of their CAF Women's Olympic qualifiers in Dire Dawa, losing 2-1 on aggregate. Needing a victory to overturn a 1-0 first-leg deficit, Rwanda travelled to Ethiopia knowing that anything less than a win would end their Olympic dream. However, the hosts struck first, leaving the visitors with an even tougher task. Ethiopia took the lead in the 28th minute through Mesay Temesgen, extending their aggregate advantage to 2-0 and putting Rwanda under pressure to respond. The goal forced André Casa Mbungo's side to push forward in search of a lifeline, but their efforts went unrewarded before the break. Emerance Niyonshuti came close to equalising in first-half stoppage time but failed to convert a one-on-one opportunity. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Trailing 2-0 on aggregate at half-time, Rwanda returned for the second half with renewed determination, taking the initiative and putting the Ethiopian defence under sustained pressure. Evelyne Ishimwe Mizero nearly reduced the deficit in the 60th minute but narrowly missed the target following a corner-kick situation. With time running out, Mbungo made tactical changes in an attempt to revive his team's hopes, introducing Josiane Uwihirwe for Régine Ihirwe in the 67th minute. The substitutions helped Rwanda maintain their attacking momentum, but Ethiopia remained resilient as they sought to protect their aggregate lead. The Amavubi continued to push forward, refusing to give up despite the mounting pressure and the diminishing time available to force a comeback. Their persistence finally paid off in the 89th minute when Ishimwe Mizero found the back of the net to make it 1-1 on the night, briefly raising hopes of a dramatic turnaround. However, the late equaliser came too late to change the outcome of the tie. Ethiopia held on to secure a 2-1 aggregate victory and advance to the next qualifying round, bringing Rwanda's campaign to an end. Ultimately, the first-leg defeat proved decisive for the Amavubi, whose late fightback in Ethiopia was not enough to keep their Los Angeles 2028 Olympic ambitions alive. Ethiopia will now face either Tanzania or Botswana in the next round as they continue their quest to qualify for the Olympic Games.
